notes.title: Custom colour palettes now available
notes.content:
The four screensavers with user-selectable colour palettes now have the option to create your own! Now you can finally create your country's flag with fish.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/4abf18c39eabdaebe407a22d519f6e7e484da6ea.png[/img]

You can add as many palettes as you want, and select whether they're enabled or disabled for if you have the 'random' palette on. You can also disable the native palettes if you want. 

Some tips-

[list]
[*] There's a maximum and minimum number of colours for each screensaver. When you create a palette, it will be set with the minimum. The maximum for most is 20, except The Sublimnotron, where there have to be three colours- no more, no less
[*] The first colour is usually the background the colour. The exception for this is The Haunted Carpet, which (for now) always has a black background
[*] Colours for fish will probably have to be relatively light, since that one has lighting applied, and the colours will spend at least some time in shadow. If the colours are too dark, they'll just show up as black, so boost the lightness a bit.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/2fe9e00ee2aa7ad6731d85a9205590b25415414f.png[/img]

Enjoy, and as ever, let me know if anything goes wrong, or you have any suggestions

Cheers,

-Ed / Jean-Paul Software

tags.feature: The four screensavers with user-selectable colour palettes now have the option to create your own!

notes.title: Minor update - Steam API is now optional
notes.content:
I've added an option to disable the Steam API, which means you can now choose whether or not you want Steam to show that you're using the software when it gets started by Windows. Note that this will also disable achievements, workshop items, any other app integrations that you have enabled (e.g. Discord), and the record of your play time.

To toggle the setting on or off, go to 'Display and Quality Settings' in the settings app, and toggle the option at the bottom labelled 'Enable Steam API', as shown here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/92f0a80a17c7866811ff308b24513e47d7f3170b.png[/img]

Any other requests, please let me know!

Cheers,

-Ed / Jean-Paul Software

P.S. please leave a review, if you can, a) to let me know what you love and hate, and b) to kick Steam's recommendation algorithm up the arse a bit.

notes.title: Version 1.0 Out Now!
notes.content:
After a long and occasionally torturous development period the Jean-Paul Software Screen Explosion is DONE. Here's a run down of everything achieved with version 1.0:

[list]
[*] 11 screensavers, most of which are good, plus a 'random' button! 
[*] No more bug reports! 
[*] Workshop support! 
[*] Over 93 copies sold!
[*] Functioning code! 
[*] PYLONS OF THE WORLD!
[*] Really cool multi-monitor support!
[*] Steam achievements!
[/list]

Thanks to everyone who has supported this so far, I love you all. I'm going to take a break and then move on to the next thing, which is a game, and probably an easier sell. Probably.

Happy screen exploding,

-Ed / Jean-Paul Software

notes.title: Minor patch, 8th November 2021
notes.content:
Now Hallowe'en is out of the way, I've added an additional mode to 'Deadline'- it can now be used to keep track of an arbitrary date and time- your birthday, the last time you had a cigarette, the amount of time left until Donald Trump returns to the White House, and so on. 

The clock will also count upwards once the date is in the past, rather than getting stuck at zero. Mechanically this makes no sense for a flip clock, but it looks a lot better.

More updates with feature requests soon, plus I'll be working on something for Christmas.

As always, let me know if there are any issues, or if there are any things you really want to see.

- Ed / Jean-Paul Software

notes.title: New Screensaver: DEADLINE
notes.content:
It's Hallowe'en, a time of creepy things, but nothing actually scary. Plastic spiders are not scary, and neither are pubs that put fake spider webs in the window. Sexy nurse can be scary, but frequently isn't; the whole cat ears thing I don't understand but I am not one to fear the incomprehensible.

But you know what is scary? Death. Specifically, [b]your[/b] death.

So! The Jean-Paul Software Screen Explosion now has a new screensaver, entitled [b]DEADLINE[/b], designed to show the passing of time and the miserable grind of life. Set it active, and you will gain an uncomfortable awareness of just how long you have left in the only world you have ever known*. Or maybe a comforting awareness- as Earl Brutus once said, life's too long.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/8576c225087574ed51378eaff033f3c4e8c9d0e3.png[/img]

Enter your birthdate, country of birth, and sex (if you choose), and the software will estimate the date of your death. Then, get a live countdown to that day, in hours, every time you view your screensaver. Or, use it to keep track of when a celebrity you hate is going to die! Or your boss, or husband, or whoever- as long as you buy the software I don't really care what you do with it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/06fb4e51e4b6a73906c89abf976bac4e3b82147c.png[/img]

Happy Hallowe'en!

- Ed / Jean-Paul Software

P.S. according to the statistics I plugged into this Rupert Murdoch should be dead right now. 

* [i]If you have solid evidence of knowing other worlds, please present it on, like, Reddit?[/i]

notes.title: The Jean-Paul Software Early Access Launch Explosion
notes.content:
Well today's the day: you can now buy The Jean-Paul Software Screen Explosion for the low price of £4 / $5 / an equivalent small amount in your local currency. I hope you like it! I fixed all the fatal bugs that I'm aware of, and there's definitely some more polishing I'd like to do, but I'd rather release at 'good enough' than 'perfect', because 'perfect' will never happen.

There's probably some bugs I've not discovered: if you see any of those, please let me know about them here: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1631280/discussions/0/5020940479392857124/

If you've any feature suggestions or ideas for improvements, please post them in the community discussions forum here: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1631280/discussions/0/

At some point I'll publish a 'road map' for improvements, but hopefully with a better name than 'road map' because that's not really very descriptive. In short, the improvements coming soon are:

- More workshop support
- Bug fixes
- A Hallowe'en screensaver
- At some point, custom fragment shaders
- A Christmas screensaver

Anyway, enjoy, and in the mean time please let me know what you like and what you don't. 

Cheers,

-Ed

notes.title: Stability improvements
notes.content:
Windows has some interesting rules about handling screensavers- namely, if they're not in [i]Windows/System32[/i] then they become somewhat flaky. Changing your power settings can cause them to vanish from the list of screensavers completely, as can temporarily turning them off; and sometimes restarting your computer can do it, and some other things I've yet to properly identify.

This update does two key things:
[list]
[*] Separates the 'screensaver' bit of the code from the 'fancy graphics' bit of the code
[*] Adds an option when setting the screensaver to copy the screensaver part to [i]Windows/System32[/i] folder
[/list]

The separation of 'fancy graphics' from 'screensaver' means we can have a small .scr file that connects to the bigger application when it needs to. Whilst I was at it I finally bit the bullet, dived into the Windows API, and implemented a preview image when viewing the screensaver:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/a1d9ebe947eb2563c4133285a1173ba8d6819ed5.png[/img]

Copying to the system folder is entirely optional, but at some point in early access I hope to get a proper install / uninstall script working that handles adding and removing this automatically. You shouldn't need to go through the process again if everything has been running properly for you; Windows will just use the updated .scr file.

Next up: more features!
